paragraphs.text: Joash reigneth well all the days of Jehoiada, 2Ch 24:1-14. He dieth; is buried honourably; and Joash falleth to idolatry; slayeth Zechariah the son of Jehoiada, 2Ch 24:15-22. He is spoiled by the Syrians; slain by Zabad and Jehozabad: Amaziah succeedeth him, 2Ch 24:23-27.
A great part of this chapter is explained on 2Ki 12.
i.e. of all the Israelites that were in the kingdom of Judah. See 2Ch 15:17 21:2. To repair the house of your God from year to year; either,
1. Repair part of it every year till the reparations be perfected; or,

2. Gather it from year to year, till you get such a sum as may suffice for the work; for he supposed one or two years’ collection would not suffice for the work, whether it were that collection of half a shekel for every man, of which see Exo 30:12,13 2Ki 12:14; or a voluntary contribution required for the present exigence of the temple by virtue of the command and example of Moses, who made such a collection for the building of the tabernacle, Exo 35:5; see also Neh 10:32; which he thought would not be any great sum, because of the great iniquity and impiety which yet had reigned for many years, and yet continued in the generality of the people of the land, the Levites not excepted, as the last clause of this verse shows.
it is observable, that he is not called the chief priest, or high priest, but only

or &c the head, which he might be in many other respects, either by reason of his near relation to the royal family; or because he was the chief of one of the twenty-four families; or because he had been the chief man in the contriving and bringing about of this great change, and the general of the forces employed about it. And the high priest seems to be mentioned as a distinct person from Jehoiada here, 2Ki 12:9,10; all which make it questionable whether Jehoiada was the high priest or no.

Heb. the collection of Moses, i.e. such a one as he commanded or made in the like case; of which See Poole "2Ch 24:5". In like manner we read of the sins of Manasseh, 2Ki 24:3, and of the sin of Jeroboam frequently.
paragraphs.anchor: The collection, according to the commandment of Moses

paragraphs.text: to wit, Ahaziah and his brethren, before they were carried away captive, 2Ch 21:17, who did this by her instigation, as this phrase implies.
both broken up the treasuries, and defaced the house itself.

i.e. A collection answerable to it; as they are said to be guilty of the error of Balaam and gainsaying of Core, Jud 1:11, who fell into sins of the same kind.
The chest was brought unto the king’s office, from the gate of the court into one of the chambers belonging to the temple, which was appointed by the king for this office.
because Athaliah and her sons had taken the old ones away, 2Ch 24:7.
paragraphs.anchor: Whereof were made vessels for the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: i.e. in Judah, which was an eminent part of Israel, and the only part of it which owned God, or was owned by God as his Israel, to whom therefore he oft appropriates this name, thereby signifying that the other tribes were unworthy of that honourable title, and had forfeited all their right in it to Judah. See Poole "2Ch 21:2".
paragraphs.anchor: He had done good in Israel

paragraphs.text: in that posture presenting their requests to him, that they might not be confined to unnecessary and troublesome journeys in coming to Jerusalem to worship, but might have the liberty which their forefathers enjoyed of worshipping God in the high places; which liberty, when once they had obtained, they knew they could then worship idols without observation or disturbance, which was the thing at which they aimed. And for the prevention of such abuses, God obliged all to worship him in one place.
By Hazael of Syria; of which see 2Ki 12:17,18
in a higher place, that his voice and message might be the better heard.
i. e. the people to whom he preached, who were easily corrupted by the examples of their apostate king and princes.

i.e. Make inquisition for my innocent blood; which he did not wish from any desire of private revenge, with which so wise and good a man would never be willing to die; but partly from a zeal to public justice, and the punishment of such gross wickedness; and partly to deter them, if possible, from completing their murderous intentions. But these words may as well be rendered indicatively as optatively,
and

so soon did God hear the cry of his holy prophet’s blood, and revenge it.

paragraphs.text: to Hazael, the king of that part of Syria called Syria Damascena, from its capital city Damascus.

i.e. of Zechariah his son; the plural number sons put for the singular son, as it is frequently, both in Scripture, as Gen 46:7 Num 26:42, and in Cicero and other profane authors. Or he might kill other sons of Jehoiada with him, either because they owned him in what he had said, or lest they should revenge his death.

paragraphs.text: either the severe prophecies against him, which are oft called burdens; of which one instance is recorded, and there might be others that are not recorded; or the great judgments of God upon him, both by the Syrians, 2Ch 24:23,24, and by great diseases, 2Ch 24:25.
